LIFTY — screen designs

Dark, warm-charcoal ground with one hot accent. Barlow Condensed for numbers, Barlow for everything else.

These solve the same problems Hevy does but the look is our own — not a copy of theirs.

Everything here is a static mockup. Tell me what to change before I build it.

The PREVIOUS column is the whole app.

Grey "17.5 kg × 8" is what you did last session, set for set. Tap it and the row fills in.

Most sets should need zero typing: tap previous, tap the check. The ±2.5 / ±1 steppers appear under the row you're editing, so you rarely open the keypad.

Sized for chalky hands mid-set:

• check box 52×44
• weight/reps fields 80×40 and 66×40
• buttons 48–52 tall

Green means one thing only — that set is banked. Nothing else in the app is green.

Your data lives on the phone and nowhere else, so the backup banner is deliberately loud once you pass a week.

CSV is for reading in Sheets. JSON is the one that can actually be restored — onto a new phone, or hers.

Deliberately absent, per your calls:

no feed, followers or sharing · no rest timer · no muscle heat map · no body measurements · no supersets or warm-up set types · no plate calculator · no RPE · no exercise illustrations (muscle chips instead)

Rest timer is the one I'd bet you end up wanting. Say the word and it goes in.

Two phones, two independent installs, no sync and no accounts.

The only thing that crosses between you is a backup file you hand over deliberately.
